Academic Regulations The fictional institution in this sample is Northbridge Institute of Technology (NIT).

The fictional institution in this sample is Northbridge Institute of Technology (NIT). Its academic year is divided into two regular semesters: Semester A and Semester B. Each semester includes teaching weeks, an assessment period, and a registration window for the next semester. The academic office publishes the exact calendar before each semester begins. Students are expected to register for the courses listed in their approved program plan. A course change is permitted only during the

Students are expected to register for the courses listed in their approved program plan. A course change is permitted only during the add/drop period and requires approval from the academic advisor. After the add/drop period closes, course changes are not normally permitted unless the Academic Registrar approves an exception in writing. A student must maintain an active registration status to attend classes, submit assessed work, and sit examinations. Students with

A student must maintain an active registration status to attend classes, submit assessed work, and sit examinations. Students with unresolved administrative holds should contact the relevant office. This document does not define every possible hold or provide an appeal timeline. Academic integrity requires students to submit their own work, acknowledge sources, and follow assessment instructions.

Academic integrity requires students to submit their own work, acknowledge sources, and follow assessment instructions. Unauthorized collaboration, plagiarism, falsification of results, or use of prohibited assistance may be referred for review. The sample policy does not specify penalty bands or an appeal procedure for integrity cases. 2. The sample assessment model uses continuous assessment and an end-semester examination. For a standard theory course, continuous assessment contributes 40% of the final course score and the end-semester examination contributes 60%. A course page may specify a different approved structure for laboratory, studio, project, or internship courses. Attendance Policy Students are expected to attend scheduled lectures, tutorials, laboratories, and other required academic activities. The minimum attendance requirement in this sample is 75% in each course. Attendance is calculated separately for each course, not as a single

semester-wide average. A student with attendance below 75% may be barred from the end-semester examination for that course. The Head of Department may review documented exceptional circumstances, but approval is not automatic. Attendance eligibility is determined using the official attendance record. Placement & Internship The Career Development Office (CDO) coordinates career workshops, employer information sessions, internship notices, and placement-related communication. Participation in these services does not guarantee an internship or job offer. To participate in the sample campus placement process, a student must be in the final year, have an active registration status, have no unresolved disciplinary restriction, and complete the CDO’s required profile form by the published deadline. Individual employers may apply additional eligibility criteria, such as degree specialization, academic score, skills, or location preferences.
